chunks: From him, from al-‘Abbās, from ‘Abd Allāh ibn al-Mughīrah, from Mu‘āwiyah ibn ‘Ammār, from Ismā‘īl ibn Yasār, who said:
I heard Abā ‘Abd Allāh عليه السلام saying:

Beware of laziness. Indeed, your Lord is Merciful and appreciates even a little. A man may perform two rak‘ahs of supererogatory prayer, seeking thereby the Face of Allah, and Allah admits him to Paradise through them. He may give a dirham in charity voluntarily, seeking thereby the Face of Allah, and Allah admits him to Paradise through it. And he may fast one day voluntarily, seeking thereby the Face of Allah, and Allah admits him to Paradise through it.

key_terms.الْجَنَّةَ: Paradise; the eternal abode of divine reward
key_terms.الْكَسَلَ: laziness; neglect and sluggishness in doing good deeds
key_terms.تَطَوُّعًا: voluntarily; an act done beyond what is obligatory
key_terms.رَحِيمٌ: Merciful; describing Allah’s mercy toward His servants
key_terms.وَجْهَ اللَّهِ: the Face of Allah; meaning Allah’s pleasure alone and sincere devotion to Him
key_terms.يَشْكُرُ الْقَلِيلَ: appreciates even a little; meaning Allah rewards small sincere deeds

ai.seo_question: How can small sincere acts of worship lead a person to Paradise?
ai.summary: This hadith warns against laziness and encourages voluntary acts of worship and charity. It teaches that Allah, in His mercy, accepts even small sincere deeds and may reward them with Paradise. The emphasis is on ikhlas—seeking the Face of Allah through even modest acts.
